statement: A contest lasts 75 minutes and has ten 3-point, ten 4-point and ten 5-point questions. Nadia plans 1.5 minutes for each 3-point question and 2.5 minutes for each 4-point question, and wants 5 minutes left at the end for checking. Sharing the rest equally, how many minutes can she plan for each 5-point question?

choices.misconception: I shared all 75 minutes equally among the 30 questions, ignoring her plan for the easier ones.
I forgot to keep the 5 minutes for checking, so I shared 35 minutes instead of 30.
I took off the checking time and the 4-point time but forgot the 15 minutes for the 3-point questions.
I shared the 70 minutes left after checking, forgetting she has already spent time on the 3-point and 4-point questions.

hints: Add up every minute that is already promised before sharing out the rest.
Time triage starts with a budget: the total time, minus the checking time, minus the planned time for the 3-point and 4-point blocks, gives the 5-point budget. Then share it equally.
The 3-point block takes 15 minutes and the 4-point block 25 minutes. With 5 minutes for checking, 30 minutes remain for ten questions.

solutions.reliable: Planned time: $10 \times 1.5 = 15$ minutes and $10 \times 2.5 = 25$ minutes, plus 5 minutes of checking, 45 minutes in all. That leaves $75 - 45 = 30$ minutes for the ten 5-point questions, so 3 minutes each. The transferable idea: a time plan is a budget, so subtract every committed minute before sharing out the rest.

whyOnTest: Planning time across the three blocks before the contest starts is a skill in itself; this checks the budget arithmetic behind a sensible plan.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
